title: Natural Domain and Range of a Quadratic Radicand
originalTopic: Functions and Graphs: Natural Domain and Range
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Determine the natural domain and range of the function g(x) = \sqrt{x^2 - 3x}.

steps.title: Formulate the Non-Negativity Condition
steps.explanation: Because the expression is governed by a square root, the quadratic radicand x^2 - 3x must be non-negative in the real number system.
steps.why: Even-degree roots require non-negative radicands to evaluate to real numbers.

steps.title: Factor the Quadratic Expression
steps.explanation: Factor out x to find the real roots of the quadratic equation x(x - 3) = 0, which are x = 0 and x = 3.
steps.why: Factoring isolates the critical boundary points where the expression can change sign.

steps.title: Perform Sign Analysis Across Intervals
steps.explanation: The critical points 0 and 3 partition the real line into three test intervals: (-inf, 0), (0, 3), and (3, inf). For x < 0, both factors are negative, so their product is positive. For 0 < x < 3, x is positive and x - 3 is negative, so their product is negative. For x > 3, both factors are positive, so their product is positive. Including endpoints gives (-inf, 0] U [3, inf).
steps.why: A continuous function changes sign only at its real roots.

steps.title: Determine the Output Range
steps.explanation: At the endpoints x = 0 and x = 3, g(0) = g(3) = 0. As x approaches positive or negative infinity, x^2 - 3x grows without bound, so sqrt(x^2 - 3x) takes all non-negative real values, [0, inf).
steps.why: The principal square root is non-negative and continuous, mapping the unbounded radicand to [0, inf).
